options: A paid Salesforce product that requires installation
A desktop app that replaces the Salesforce database
A free, browser-based tool for querying and working with Salesforce data
A feature that only exists inside Data Loader
questions.explain: Workbench is a free, web-based tool that connects to your org with no installation.

questions.q: What is one clear advantage of Workbench over Data Loader?
options: It needs no installation; it runs in a browser
It always handles far larger volumes
It runs on a schedule from the command line
It is officially supported like a core Salesforce feature
questions.explain: No install is a real convenience; volume and scheduled jobs remain Data Loader strengths.

questions.q: Which Workbench menu holds the SOQL Query page?
options: Migration
Info only
Utilities only
Queries
questions.explain: SOQL Query and SOSL Search live under the Queries menu.

questions.q: Which of these data operations does Workbench's Data menu offer?
options: Only Export
Insert, Update, Upsert, Delete, Undelete and Purge
Only Insert
Only Hard Delete
questions.explain: The Data menu covers the main DML-style operations, including Undelete and Purge.

questions.q: What should you keep in mind about Workbench's support status?
options: It is guaranteed by a Salesforce SLA
It can only connect to sandboxes
It is a community tool, not an officially supported Salesforce product, so check your org's security policy
It stores your data permanently on its own servers
questions.explain: Workbench is community maintained, so treat it accordingly and follow your organization's rules.
